mechanism_narrative: Persistent RESIDENTIAL elevation (11-13% above baseline) combined with stable RETAIL_REC depression (-33 to -39%) indicates lockdown-like confinement. As confinement duration extends into week 5-8, behavioral fatigue and essential-goods depletion will force retail visits upward, reversing the current decline.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over weeks t+1 to t+4 remains below -30% or declines further relative to the t-4 to t-0 mean of -33.4%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has collapsed to -34 to -40% and shows no recovery trend across four weeks. Sustained transit avoidance signals persistent fear of public transport. This will suppress retail visits that depend on transit access, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed below current levels over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for all four observed weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -37.7, -34.7, -40.4, -38.7 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -25% in any single week during t+1 to t+4, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -25%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stabilized at -3.9 to -9.7%, showing minimal week-on-week volatility. This stability signals that essential shopping routines are locked in. Discretionary retail (RETAIL_REC) will remain suppressed because consumers are rationing trips and bundling essential and discretionary purchases, preventing standalone retail visits.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM coefficient of variation < 0.15 over prior 4 weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2% while RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -25% in any week during t+1 to t+2.

mechanism_narrative: November 15 marks the onset of pre-holiday shopping season in Madrid. Despite current restrictions, pent-up holiday demand will overcome behavioral suppression over the next 4 weeks, driving RETAIL_REC upward as consumers front-load gift purchases before potential December lockdowns.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2020-11-15, start of holiday shopping season
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over t+1 to t+4 is lower than or equal to the t-4 to t-0 mean of -33.4%, or shows monotonic decline week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES have declined to -26.9 to -34.0%, indicating remote-work enforcement or business closures. If WORKPLACES remain below -25% over the next week, it signals sustained policy restrictions. Under sustained restrictions, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as non-essential retail closures or capacity limits persist.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -25% in week t+1
failure_condition: WORKPLACES recovers above -20% in week t+1 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -20%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined from -33.1% to -20.0% over four weeks, showing a +13.1 percentage-point recovery trend. This signals emerging outdoor-activity tolerance. If this trend continues, consumers will substitute indoor retail with outdoor recreation, further depressing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS week-on-week change is positive for 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS trend from -33.1 to -20.0 is +13.1 points over 4 weeks
failure_condition: PARKS declines below -20% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC rises above -25% while PARKS continues to recover.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-34 to -40%), WORKPLACES (-27 to -34%), and RESIDENTIAL (+10 to +13%) form a coherent lockdown signature. The joint persistence of all three signals over four weeks indicates regime stability. Under stable lockdown, RETAIL_REC will remain anchored near current levels (-33%) with no significant recovery, as the underlying mobility constraint is structural.
candidate_trigger: all three proxies remain within their observed ranges (TRANSIT < -30%, WORKPLACES < -20%, RESIDENTIAL > 9%)
evidence_refs: fact:all three series show stable patterns across 4 weeks
failure_condition: Any one of the three proxies breaks its observed range in week t+1, and RETAIL_REC simultaneously rises above -25%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained stable at -3.9 to -9.7% while RETAIL_REC has remained stable at -32.3 to -38.4%. The tight correlation and mutual stability suggest consumers have adapted to a new equilibrium of restricted mobility. This equilibrium will persist over the next two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC within -30 to -36% range.
candidate_trigger: correlation between GROCERY_PHARM and RETAIL_REC week-on-week changes is positive and > 0.5
evidence_refs: fact:both series show low volatility and stable negative levels
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -25% in any week during t+1 to t+2 while GROCERY_PHARM remains between -3 and -10%.
